title: reading-notes-llm-inference-samira-khan
content:
Quick reading notes: LLM inference optimizations and practical experiments

Context / goal:
- Capture practical takeaways from recent papers/blogs I read while setting up experiments for latency-sensitive endpoints on Redwood Dedicated. Focus is on: quantization accuracy vs perf, KV-cache management, batching strategies, and graceful degradation/fallbacks.
- Notes are messy — TODO: turn into a short runbook for the infra/serving team.

FlashAttention & kernel-level optimizations
- FlashAttention (and FlashAttention2 followups) gives huge memory and perf wins for long sequences by reordering compute to avoid large intermediate mats. In practice: big win for 8k+ context windows where GEMM memory blows up.
- Implementation notes: needs attention to kernel compatibility and CUDA/toolkit versions. Check Triton vs custom CUDA kernels tradeoffs.
- Action: prototype with a 13B model on a p4d-like machine and measure tokens/sec for context lengths [512, 2048, 8192]. Compare Triton implementation vs vendor kernels.

Quantization (GPTQ / 4-bit / groupwise)
- GPTQ-style post-training quantization gives near-fp16 perplexity for many models at 4-bit. Key caveats: per-channel/group quantization and reconstruction of outlier weights matter a lot.
- QAT (quant-aware finetune) better but expensive; GPTQ often "good enough" for inference-optimized models.
- Observe degradation patterns: space of prompts where quantization hurts (long-context summarization, numeric reasoning). Need targeted eval sets.
- Action: run GPTQ on 7B & 13B; compare generation quality (ROUGE/BLEU) and hallucination rate on our eval prompts.

KV cache management and eviction policies
- KV cache reduces compute for autoregressive decoding but memory blowup for many concurrent sessions / long contexts. Two axes: per-request cache size + global memory cap.
- Eviction strategies: LRU across sessions, prefix hashing (shared prefixes reuse same KV), and partial recomputation (drop older tokens and recompute when needed).
- For Redwood Dedicated: consider hybrid approach — keep hot sessions pinned (by SLA), best-effort eviction for low-tier. Also explore prefix-sharing via request routing to reuse cached prefixes (requires deterministic tokenization & canonical promptization).
- Action: instrument cache hit/miss, distribution of session lengths, and ratio of prefix reuse.

Batching and dynamic batching policies
- Continuous batching is best for throughput but harms p95 latency. Need policies that adapt to SLO: e.g., max-delay-scheduler where small delay (2–5ms) and size threshold yields most of the throughput gains with reasonable p95.
- Consider model-splitting: faster small-model fallback for sub-threshold requests vs enqueue to large-model for high-quality outputs.

Quality monitoring and evals
- Always tie quantization/optimization changes to a small but representative eval set (prompt suite). We should run both synthetic and customer-like prompts. Track metrics: avg token time, p50/p95 latency, top-1 edit distance vs baseline, and hallucination flags.
- Experiments to add: compare regressed metrics after 4-bit conversion per prompt cluster (chat, instruction, code).

Operational notes / TODOs
- Create an eval job in infra that can A/B: baseline fp16 vs 4-bit GPTQ vs 8-bit. Store outputs + generation seeds for deterministic comparisons.
- Add KV-cache metrics to Console: session-length histogram, memory-per-session, prefix-hit-rate.
- Prototype FlashAttention3 kernel fallback for cases where Triton not available.
- Draft a short runbook for Dedicated customers about "recommended configs" (batching window, quantization profiles, pin hot sessions).

Open questions / uncertainties
- How to best surface per-customer cost/latency tradeoff in Console? (slider that toggles quantization/profile and shows expected p95/cost?)
- Is it feasible to do localized QAT for high-value customers (few-shot finetune to regain quality lost by quantization)?
- How to safely route requests to smaller models as graceful degradation without big UX regressions?

References and quick links (for follow-up):
- FlashAttention paper + impl (see linked artifacts)
- GPTQ implementations and notes (linked)
- DeepSpeed Inference docs for kernel selection and tensor parallelism

Notes to self:
- Keep these notes short and move most ops steps into a dedicated Confluence page.
- Sync with Ethan and Lena next week to align on which prototype to run first (13B FlashAttention + GPTQ seems highest ROI).

End of file.
